Assertions.Description: In a clean authorized installation, Power Display defaults to disabled.
Cancel the Settings enable warning; UI and saved enabled state remain disabled.
Accept the Settings enable warning; saved enabled state and resident process become enabled.
Disable through Settings; the resident process exits and saved state agrees; restore original enablement.
With the enabled module ready, Settings launch opens the flyout.
With the enabled module ready, the real Quick Access entry opens the flyout.
With the enabled module ready and tray icon visible, clicking the actual tray icon opens the flyout.
With compatible foreground integrity, the current configured shortcut opens the flyout.
With no existing module instance, launching the installed GUI without Runner arguments shows its standalone window.
Cancel a shortcut draft without changing the saved original modifiers/key.
Save an unused valid binding; every modifier/key persists and the new binding toggles the flyout.
After saving the new binding, the old binding no longer activates Power Display.
Restore the original binding through Settings and observe its actual activation.
Escape in the foreground flyout hides its window while the module process remains resident.
Moving focus from the flyout to an owned ordinary window hides the flyout without terminating the module.
Reopen with the same tested trigger; the flyout is usable and no extra resident instance accumulates.
Changing tray-icon visibility in Settings changes the actual tray entry and can be restored.
With saved profiles, profile-switcher visibility controls the flyout button; restore the original option.
Identify-button visibility controls the refresh menu's identify entry and can be restored.
With real monitors, identify overlays show each correct display number on its display and close afterward.
On two differently scaled displays including non-primary/negative coordinates, repeated flyout entry stays within the target work area without taskbar overlap or clipped controls.
Invoke the real flyout refresh menu; observe discovery completing and current controls returning, not merely command acceptance.
When no controllable monitor is present, settled discovery shows a no-monitors state without fabricated hardware controls.
On an authorized hardware setup, unplug/reconnect triggers discovery after the configured delay and returns the current display set.
On an authorized display-sleep setup, wake disables stale interaction during discovery and restores current monitor controls afterward.
Across rediscovery/reordering, stable device/port identities preserve the correct physical monitor's preferences, including identical models.
A WMI-brightness-capable panel has localized Built-in Display identity, working brightness with independent readback, and no duplicate DDC controls.
On a dual-GPU laptop with its internal panel driven by the discrete GPU, WMI capability still permits detection and brightness control.
Supported per-monitor control options change the flyout; unsupported feature options stay unavailable.
Hide/unhide a monitor through Settings; only that monitor's flyout visibility changes.
Monitor preferences survive Settings reopening and rediscovery.
With file-write/event instrumentation, only seven user-editable monitor preferences cause save then IPC then module-event; runtime/derived notifications and disk reload do not write back.
On a newly discovered compatible monitor input-source control defaults off; cancel enable and it stays off.
Accept input-source enable; the option persists and supported control appears; restore the option without switching hardware.
On a newly discovered compatible monitor color-temperature control defaults off; cancel enable and it stays off.
Accept color-temperature enable; the option persists and supported control appears; restore the option without changing hardware.
On a newly discovered compatible monitor power-state control defaults off; cancel enable and it stays off.
Accept power-state enable; the option persists and supported control appears; restore the option without changing hardware.
On supported hardware, a distinct safe brightness edit reaches only the intended monitor and independent hardware readback confirms change and restoration.
On supported hardware, a distinct safe contrast edit reaches only the intended monitor and independent hardware readback confirms change and restoration.
On supported hardware, initial volume reflects the successful device read; a safe edit and restoration are confirmed by independent hardware readback without changing another monitor.
Mouse drag of each available brightness/contrast/volume slider reaches hardware after settling.
Keyboard arrows on each available brightness/contrast/volume slider reach hardware after settling.
With a touchscreen, both drag and tap-on-track on each available slider reach hardware after settling.

For each available slider and increment 1,2,5,10,15,20,25, both wheel directions change hardware by that step without parent scrolling; safe instrumented boundaries clamp at 0/100 and tray-wheel Off does not disable sliders.
On an instrumented DDC fixture with non-100 brightness maximum, 0/50/100 percent map to the native range; UI/storage stay percentages and original hardware is restored.
On an instrumented DDC fixture with non-100 contrast maximum, 0/50/100 percent map to the native range; UI/storage stay percentages and original hardware is restored.
On an instrumented DDC fixture with non-100 volume maximum, 0/50/100 percent map to the native range; UI/storage stay percentages and original hardware is restored.
With an advertised safe input and physical recovery, select input source and independently verify the actual input, then restore it.
With advertised color presets and physical recovery, select a preset and independently verify hardware, then restore it.
With a secondary recoverable DDC-wake-capable monitor, standby changes hardware and selecting On wakes it; restore its original power state.
On an authorized disposable secondary display, shipped CLI orientation 0/90/180/270 matches Windows display configuration and can be restored; no absent flyout rotation-button requirement.
With at least two brightness-capable monitors, linking seeds the master from the linked monitor with lowest Windows display number.
Master brightness changes all included monitors with independent hardware readback; individual cards remain expandable.
An excluded monitor does not follow the master and retains its working independent slider.
Linked mode and stable-ID exclusions survive reopen/restart; a newly connected monitor is included unless excluded.
Applying a per-monitor profile turns linking off before applying distinct per-monitor hardware values.
With tray mode Off, wheel over the icon leaves brightness and ordinary wheel delivery unchanged.
Primary display mode adjusts only the eligible primary monitor without opening the flyout.
All displays mode adjusts eligible visible brightness monitors and excludes hidden/unreadable targets without opening the flyout.
Tray wheel uses the configured increment and clamps at safe instrumented boundaries; restore mode and hardware.
With a controllable monitor, create an owned named profile and reopen its exact selected fields/values.
Cancel both a new-profile draft and an existing owned-profile edit without persistence changes.
Rename an owned profile while retaining its stable ID and creation time.
Two profiles with the same name retain distinct stable numeric IDs.
Cancel deletion and retain the exact selected owned profile.
Confirm deletion of one owned ID; unrelated profiles remain unchanged.
An invalid empty name or empty selection cannot be saved as a new profile.
Settings Apply for an owned profile changes its included monitor fields as verified on hardware.
Selecting an owned profile from the flyout changes its included monitor fields as verified on hardware.
Profile application preserves omitted fields and unrelated monitors, retaining distinct per-monitor values; restore pre-test hardware.
Rename/save an owned profile with a missing monitor; retain its saved row, fields, ID and creation time.
Rename/save with temporarily unavailable capabilities or unsupported saved color presets; retain original included fields.
Explicitly deselect a preserved monitor or field; remove only that selection.
Same-size capability name/value updates refresh the editor; cleared selections, restored support and selected color values stay consistent; newly chosen unsupported values cannot be saved.
Move the middle of three owned profiles up/down via menu; persisted order changes without changing IDs, creation times or monitor settings.
In ordinary Settings, drag an owned profile to another position and verify order after reopening without changing profile identity/content.
Flyout, CLI profiles and Light Switch pickers use the same persisted order; restore the original ordering.
In an authorized elevated Settings session, dragging is disabled with guidance while Move up/down remains usable.
Add, edit and delete owned input-source/color-preset mappings; exact code/value/name persists and deletion removes only the owned mapping.
Cancel new/edit mapping drafts without saving changes.
On matching hardware, a global mapping renames the advertised value across applicable monitors without changing its VCP value; deletion restores the normal label.
On matching hardware, a monitor-specific mapping affects only its target identity and leaves other monitors' labels/values unchanged.
With authorized theme changes and two owned profiles, successive light/dark transitions apply the matching hardware values, including the second hotkey transition.
Rename/reorder preserves stable profile associations; deleting an assigned owned profile clears its reference.
When Power Display is disabled, Light Switch configuration shows its warning rather than implying successful apply; restore theme/bindings/profiles/hardware.
On recoverable hardware, startup with restoration off does not replay saved values.
On recoverable hardware, startup with restoration on restores saved supported values.
With an isolated state fixture, null/unread saved values are not applied as zero, while a genuine saved zero remains valid.
With an instrumented failed initial read and saved value equal to its displayed placeholder, restore still sends the hardware write.
A final edit survives cooperative exit/reopen in valid monitor-state storage; restore original startup behavior and hardware.
Cancel compatibility warning without enabling; acceptance enables it and triggers rediscovery.
On an instrumented empty/unparsable-capabilities monitor, compatibility mode recovers supported continuous controls without exposing unsupported brightness.
On an instrumented transient failure, bounded retries recover and successful probe readings initialize UI rather than being replaced by failed rereads.
A valid cached VCP reading supports later compatibility discovery for the same stable identity; never-successful or different-device data cannot fabricate support.
In an isolated upgrade fixture, Settings/profiles/state legacy monitor IDs migrate only on exact EDID/display-number matches; ambiguous/unmatched entries do not attach to another monitor.
In an isolated upgrade fixture, name-addressed profiles and Light Switch references migrate to stable numeric IDs without losing valid associations.
With an instrumented clock/discovery fixture, absent recent entries retain preferences, stale entries expire under the retention rule, and hidden entries remain.
In an explicitly authorized disposable fault fixture, an orphan discovery marker auto-disables before DDC access and locks Settings; Ignore clears the warning without silently enabling.
An instrumented blacklisted monitor identity is excluded before capability access; do not attach known-bad hardware to provoke a crash.
Normal tray Exit releases the exact owned module process, tray icon and CLI service.
With a controlled discovery-in-progress fixture, cooperative exit leaves no false crash marker and next launch does not auto-disable.
Installed CLI help/version reports usable command syntax and its actual version.
CLI list returns identities/transports matching actual discovery, including an empty result when no controllable monitor exists.
With real monitors, CLI get retains supported/unread distinctions rather than presenting a placeholder as a read.
With a capable monitor, CLI capabilities reports its advertised values.
CLI profiles returns saved owned profile IDs and display order.
With distinguishable monitors, number and stable-ID selectors resolve correctly; stable ID wins when both are supplied.
The installed native shim forwards arguments and the resulting CLI exit code.
On recoverable hardware, CLI set reaches each supported continuous/discrete setting and orientation, independently observed on the intended target.
CLI up/down uses explicit step or configured wheel increment, including zero-step no-op and clamping; observe actual hardware.
With multiple recoverable monitors, duplicate monitor-number selectors apply each target once and preserve per-target success/failure reporting.
CLI apply-profile uses the owned stable numeric ID and applies its hardware settings.
Without --confirm-power-off a standby/off request is rejected without hardware change; authorized confirmed action follows the physical recovery plan.
An unknown monitor request yields exit 1 without hardware writes.
A continuous value outside 0..100 yields exit 2 without hardware writes.
On an appropriate capability fixture, a discrete value not advertised yields exit 3 without hardware writes.
On an appropriate monitor fixture, an unsupported feature yields exit 4 without hardware writes.
A request requiring a monitor selector but missing it yields exit 6 without hardware writes.
Parse errors, negative step, malformed monitor-number lists and multiple setting options yield exit 7 without hardware writes; observe every matrix input.
On a controlled hardware fixture only, hardware failure yields exit 5 rather than fabricated success.
On a controlled IPC fixture only, request timeout yields exit 8 rather than fabricated success.
On a controlled IPC fixture only, internal error yields exit 9 rather than fabricated success.
With the provider absent, a CLI request reports ProviderUnavailable and exit 10 without starting the provider.
Default read output remains text; --json read results are compact JSON Lines on stdout.
For an authorized hardware mutation, --json result is compact JSON Lines on stdout with independently confirmed hardware behavior.
Structured parse errors are JSON Lines on stderr with matching exit codes and no mixed human stdout.
Structured IPC errors are JSON Lines on stderr with matching exit codes and no mixed human stdout.
Global --json before/after a subcommand does not consume its argument; help/version keep documented human-readable behavior.
In an authorized policy fixture, forced-disabled prevents Settings enable and direct GUI activation.
In an authorized policy fixture, forced-enabled produces policy-controlled Settings state.
Returning to Not configured restores normal user control; restore exact original policy existence/kind and runtime state.
With authorized theme changes, light/dark flyout, Settings and dialogs remain readable and unclipped.
In another installed locale, UI/Built-in Display labels localize while Power Display and CLI syntax literals remain intact; restore original language/theme.
OOBE presents the correct module identity and current configured shortcut; restore original visible UI.
For an advertised VCP-capable monitor, Settings details match independently captured capability code names/values.
Copy the selected monitor's VCP list with a private complete clipboard guard; verify owned copied text and restore all original formats.
Navigate away/return while the module runs, change an owned non-hardware option and observe usable controls, persistence and flyout update; restore it without duplicate runtime-notification saves.
